# Weekly Meal Plan Budget Check

This plan is **close to realistic for a family of four on $180**, assuming you already have basics like oil, salt, pepper, and a few spices. The main pressure points are **salmon**, **fresh produce overlap**, and **buying separate proteins** for the vegetarian adult.

# Meal-by-Meal Adjustments and Cost Outlook

| Day | Original Meal | Suggested Adjustment | Cost Impact | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | Pasta primavera | Keep it, use seasonal veg and add white beans or chickpeas | Lower | Good low-cost start; easy vegetarian fit |
| Tuesday | Chicken rice bowls | Use chicken for most, tofu or extra beans for vegetarian adult | Neutral to lower | Make one base bowl for all, then split toppings |
| Wednesday | Lentil curry | Keep it, serve with rice and yogurt | Lower | Strong budget meal; make extra for leftovers |
| Thursday | Tacos | Use black beans + seasoned turkey or chicken option | Lower | Easy to customize for vegetarian and child |
| Friday | Salmon with potatoes | Swap salmon for baked tilapia, canned tuna patties, or sheet-pan chicken | Lower | Biggest budget saver if salmon is expensive |
| Saturday | Vegetable stir-fry | Keep it, add noodles or rice and use leftover vegetables | Lower | Best day to clear fridge odds and ends |
| Sunday | Soup and sandwiches | Make a big-pot soup and use leftover bread/veg/protein | Lower | Good cleanup meal and low waste |

## Best Substitutions to Fit the Household

- **Vegetarian adult:** Use tofu, beans, lentils, eggs, or cheese as the default protein add-on.
- **Child who dislikes mushrooms:** Replace mushrooms with zucchini, bell peppers, carrots, spinach, broccoli, or peas.
- **Salmon night:** If the budget feels tight, switch to:
  - baked chicken thighs
  - white fish on sale
  - tuna cakes
  - chickpea patties for a vegetarian version
- **Pasta primavera:** Skip mushrooms entirely and lean on carrots, peas, broccoli, and peppers.
- **Tacos:** Build a shared taco bar with one meat filling and one bean filling so everyone eats the same sides.

## Waste-Reduction Plan

- Use the **same vegetables across 3–4 meals**: onions, carrots, bell peppers, broccoli, spinach.
- Buy **one large bag of rice** and **one pasta shape** to support multiple dinners.
- Cook **extra lentils, rice, and roasted vegetables** to reuse in bowls, tacos, or soup.
- Turn leftover chicken, beans, or vegetables into:
  - soup on Sunday
  - sandwich filling
  - lunch wraps
  - fried rice or stir-fry
- Plan **one “clean-out-the-fridge” meal** before shopping for the next week.

## Budget Reality Check

Estimated weekly grocery cost for this menu:
- Produce: **$45–$60**
- Grains, pasta, bread, tortillas: **$25–$35**
- Proteins: **$45–$65**
- Dairy, sauces, canned goods, extras: **$25–$35**

Estimated total: **$140–$195**

### Bottom line
- **Yes, $180 is realistic** if you:
  - keep salmon modest or replace it
  - use beans/lentils/tofu often
  - buy seasonal produce
  - reuse ingredients across meals
- **No, it gets tight** if you buy premium proteins, lots of packaged snacks, or multiple specialty vegetarian substitutes.
